trend-analysis.name: Trend Analysis
trend-analysis.summary: Identify and discuss data-driven patterns to understand performance and forecast what's next. Useful for market reviews, strategic outlooks, and any deck where the audience must act on a direction-of-travel call.

beats.name: Introduction
beats.description: Open by establishing why this trend matters now. Tie it to a decision on the table or a forecast that's about to be made. Trends without consequences are filler.

beats.name: Historical Comparison
beats.description: Contrast current data with the relevant past. Pick the comparison window that makes the trend visible without cherry-picking. Be honest about base effects.

beats.name: Pattern Identification
beats.description: Name the recurring outcome you've spotted. Use one or two strong charts that show the pattern unambiguously. Avoid overclaiming significance from a small N.

beats.name: Future Prediction
beats.description: Project where the trend leads if it continues. Show the forecast and the confidence interval. State the assumptions that would have to break for the prediction to fail.

beats.name: Action Plan
beats.description: Translate the prediction into the strategy it implies. Specific actions, sequenced. Each action should map to a particular reading of the trend, not a generic best practice.

beats.name: Implementation
beats.description: Walk through how the actions get executed: owners, milestones, monitoring. The audience should leave understanding what to do tomorrow, not just what to think about.

beats.name: Conclusion
beats.description: Recap the trend, the forecast, and the recommended action. End with the leading indicator you'll watch to know if the call is right.

marketing.name: Marketing
marketing.summary: Marketing professionals analyzing campaign performance, brand metrics, and growth strategies.
marketing.description: Marketing professionals reviewing campaign performance, brand metrics, and growth strategy. Make the funnel visible, highlight engagement metrics, keep the brand consistent, and tell the story visually. Moderate chart density; 15-30 slides.

align.name: Align
align.summary: Create shared understanding and commitment across people who need to move together.
align.description: Use when stakeholders need a common view of goals, constraints, priorities, or responsibilities. Emphasize shared language, explicit tradeoffs, and next steps.
align.outcome: Stakeholders leave with the same priorities and operating assumptions.
successCriteria: Owners and next steps are clear

technical.name: Technical
technical.summary: Precise, evidence-led voice for engineering, research, and product-detail audiences.
technical.description: Lead with the question or claim, then walk through the mechanism and the numbers. Use exact terminology; assume the audience can handle and prefers it. Diagrams, tables, and benchmarks are first-class.
voiceCues: State the claim, then the mechanism, then the evidence.
Use exact terminology — don't soften technical terms for general readability.
Quote benchmarks with conditions (cold/warm, p50/p95/p99, dataset, hardware).
Prefer diagrams and tables over prose paragraphs for structural information.
samplePhrases: p95 inference latency is 38ms on a single A100, down from 312ms on the prior runtime.
We replaced the streaming serializer with a batched protobuf path; throughput rose 4.2× under load.
The result holds for context windows up to 32k tokens; beyond that, see appendix B.

dark.name: Dark
dark.description: A rich dark-mode theme with bold contrast and modern style. Great for moody, high-impact presentations.

deep-purple.name: Deep Purple
deep-purple.summary: Purple-led palette for innovation and premium positioning.
deep-purple.description: A focused purple palette for decks that need to feel creative, distinctive, and premium.

boost.name: Boost
boost.summary: High-energy digital accents for demos and launch moments.
boost.description: A vivid blue-red digital palette with bright chart accents. Best for product stories that need strong on-screen presence.

aparajita.name: Aparajita
aparajita.description: Aparajita is a sans serif OPF font scheme for complex script presentations, using Aparajita for both headings and body text.

seaford.name: Seaford
seaford.description: Seaford is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Seaford Display for headings with Seaford for body text.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.
